# utmp fixtures

These are **real** utmp files, written by the C library's own `pututline()`
inside a container — not synthesised by netra. A fixture generated by the code
under test would validate nothing, since any layout mistake would be made
identically on both sides.

## Provenance

| File | Image | libc | Platform | `sizeof(struct utmp)` | Bytes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `glibc-amd64.utmp` | `debian:bookworm-slim` | glibc 2.36 | `linux/amd64` | 384 | 2688 |
| `glibc-arm64.utmp` | `debian:bookworm-slim` | glibc 2.36 | `linux/arm64` | 400 | 2800 |

Both contain the same seven records in this order:

| # | `ut_type` | value | counted? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `RUN_LVL` | 1 | no |
| 2 | `BOOT_TIME` | 2 | no |
| 3 | `LOGIN_PROCESS` | 6 | no |
| 4 | `USER_PROCESS` | 7 | **yes** |
| 5 | `USER_PROCESS` | 7 | **yes** |
| 6 | `USER_PROCESS` | 7 | **yes** |
| 7 | `DEAD_PROCESS` | 8 | no |

A correct reader counts exactly **3**. The non-`USER_PROCESS` records are the
point of the fixture: counting records instead of sessions gives 7, and a
getty waiting on an empty tty (`LOGIN_PROCESS`) is nobody logged in.

## Why two architectures

`sizeof(struct utmp)` is not constant, which is the single most dangerous
assumption in this parser:

|  | amd64 | arm64 |
|---|---|---|
| glibc | 384 | 400 |
| musl | 400 | 400 |

x86-64 defines `__WORDSIZE_TIME64_COMPAT32`, so glibc keeps `ut_session` and
`ut_tv` 32-bit there; aarch64 does not. The size therefore depends on the
**host's** libc and word size, which a statically linked agent reading a
bind-mounted `/var/run/utmp` cannot know at build time. `users.go` detects it
per file instead, and these two fixtures are what prove the detection works
rather than accidentally agreeing with one machine.

## musl writes nothing

musl's `pututline()` is a no-op stub: the same generator produced a **0-byte**
file on Alpine. There is deliberately no musl fixture, because there is no
such thing as a musl-written utmp. On those systems the file is absent or
empty and the collector reports `users=unavailable` — which is why that path
is the common case rather than the exotic one.

## Regenerating

```c
/* gen.c — build with: gcc gen.c -o gen */
#include <string.h>
#include <utmp.h>

static void put(short type, int pid, const char *line, const char *id,
                const char *user, const char *host) {
    struct utmp u;
    memset(&u, 0, sizeof(u));
    u.ut_type = type;
    u.ut_pid = pid;
    strncpy(u.ut_line, line, sizeof(u.ut_line) - 1);
    strncpy(u.ut_id,   id,   sizeof(u.ut_id)   - 1);
    strncpy(u.ut_user, user, sizeof(u.ut_user) - 1);
    strncpy(u.ut_host, host, sizeof(u.ut_host) - 1);
    u.ut_tv.tv_sec = 1700000000;
    pututline(&u);
}

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
    if (argc < 2) return 1;
    utmpname(argv[1]);          /* the file must already exist:  */
    setutent();                 /* pututline opens without O_CREAT */
    put(RUN_LVL,       0,    "~",     "~~",   "runlevel", "");
    put(BOOT_TIME,     0,    "~",     "~~",   "reboot",   "");
    put(LOGIN_PROCESS, 900,  "tty2",  "tty2", "LOGIN",    "");
    put(USER_PROCESS,  1001, "tty1",  "tty1", "jan",      "");
    put(USER_PROCESS,  1002, "pts/0", "ts/0", "jan",      "10.0.0.5");
    put(USER_PROCESS,  1003, "pts/1", "ts/1", "root",     "10.0.0.6");
    put(DEAD_PROCESS,  1004, "pts/2", "ts/2", "",         "");
    endutent();
    return 0;
}
```

```sh
docker run --rm --platform linux/amd64 -v "$PWD":/w -w /w debian:bookworm-slim sh -c '
  apt-get update -qq && apt-get install -y -qq gcc &&
  gcc gen.c -o /tmp/gen && : > glibc-amd64.utmp && /tmp/gen glibc-amd64.utmp'
```
